PREFACE TO FIRST EDITION

In Opening schools among the Garos. who had no written 
language, the supply of text-books was one of the first problems A 
few books in Garos foi biginners ha\e been prepared by American 
Baptist Missionanes, and are mostly in use An Arithmetic thus 
prepared was destroyed by fire and has not yet been replaced The 
Missionaries few in number and buidened with a great variety of 
work, have not been able to give as much time as they would like to 
the prepEU-ation of Garo text-books For this reason as well as the 
fact that educated Garos should know Bengali the language of their 
educated neighbours it has been found necessaiy as well as wise to 
use Bengali text-books as a mtdiuin of instruction To use these a 
Bengali-Garo Dictionaiy seemed to be almost one of the first needs 
I therefore instructed Rev Ramkhe one of our mission employees 
to give a portion of his lime to preparing Garo definitions to a Bengali 
vocabulary This he began in 1877 and he had the present work 
completed in 1881 It was tlu-n put to pi ess in Calcutta But the 
difficulties of supc nntending the printing at so great a distance with 
no one at ( he press who understood the Cjaro language has made its 
progress slow Moreover, the Missionaries Rev EG Phillips and 
myself have at times through absence, been obliged to delay the 
work Garo proof rciders have been tiained but either death or 
icmovals have always prevented their continued assistance Thus 
the editing and proof reading has been extended over a period of six 
years dunng whi< h the adaptation of the Bengali tharacter to the 
Garo language was in a state of growth and subject to frequent 
changes

While it would be impossible to give all the terms to be found in 
the vanous dialects the author has aimed at giving the definitions 
in the different leading dialects Many of the moie familiar Bengali 
words are often used in the definitions - usually bracketed Garoized 
Bengali woids are also frequent Notwithstanding these difficulties, 
and the apparent inconsistencies to be found in the book, we think 
there will be no difficulty m reading and readily understanding the 
definitions, and that the book is well adapted to the purpose for 
which it was made viz . for the use of Garo pupils in learning the 
meaning of Bengali words

Tura, Garo Hdls, Assarth 
September, 1887

M.C. BfASON.
